messages.subject: [statnet_help] Announcing LOLOG: A New Generative Statistical Model for Graphs
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Announcing LOLOG: A New Generative Statistical Model for Graphs
messages.body_plain:
Dear statnet community,

I am happy to announce the first public release of a new model class for network analysis, which we call the Latent Order Logistic (LOLOG) graph model. LOLOGs are a fully general class of probability models that are complimentary to ERGMs. Like ERGMs, terms modeling different important network features can be mixed and matched to provide a rich generative description of complex networks. LOLOGs show considerable models stability, avoiding the computational complexities of MCMC sampling and the modeling challenges posed by phase transitions (a.k.a. degeneracy).

A package implementing the model is available at 

https://github.com/statnet/lolog

and includes links to a technical paper as well as introductory vignettes to get you started.

This class is particularly appropriate for networks that undergo growth. For example, citation networks, where papers are sequentially added and form ties to existing publications. We?d be very interested to hear feedback from the community either on list or off, especially if you are working with a network that has a plausible growth process underlying it and/or is difficult to fit with existing model classes.

Sincerely,
Ian Fellows
ian@fellstat.com

messages.body_plain:
Dear Pavel,

I tried other strategies on bootstrapping, like putting boot.R in the control.ergm.ego(), increasing number of boot.R, and adding node attributes and node match terms, the error still exists. It seems whatever number I increase for the bootstrap, for instance, 20000, the time of model running dose not change. I thought that as the number of bootstrap increase, the time for model running would increase dramatically. This got me think whether the bootstrap is functional in my code? 

Meanwhile, when I put node match terms into the model to test the differential homophily, another error popped up repeatedly (age is a 3-level factor, acadegree and marrital are 2-level factors ):

> advice.fit.diffhomo=ergm.ego(advice~edges+nodefactor("age")+nodefactor("acadegree")+nodefactor("marrital")+nodematch("age",diff=T)+nodematch("acadegree",diff=T)+nodematch("marrital",diff=T),control=control.ergm.ego(ppopsize=2000,stats.est="bootstrap",boot.R=20000))
Constructing pseudopopulation network.
Note: Constructed network has size 1995, different from requested 2000. Estimation should not be meaningfully affected.
Unable to match target stats. Using MCMLE estimation.
Starting maximum likelihood estimation via MCMLE:
Iteration 1 of at most 20:
Optimizing with step length 1.
The log-likelihood improved by 0.3384.
Step length converged once. Increasing MCMC sample size.
Iteration 2 of at most 20:
Optimizing with step length 1.
The log-likelihood improved by 0.6509.
Step length converged twice. Stopping.
This model was fit using MCMC.  To examine model diagnostics and check for degeneracy, use the mcmc.diagnostics() function.
Error in solve.default(DtDe) : 
  system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 4.12265e-18

I realize that this error is related to the linear dependency among the terms, so I decreased the number of the terms in varying combinations. So the age model worked fine:
> social.fit.diffhomo=ergm.ego(social~edges+nodefactor("age")+nodematch("age",diff=T),control=control.ergm.ego(ppopsize=2000,stats.est="bootstrap?,boot.R=20000))

but the acadegree model and the marrital model did not work, showing the above ?system is computationally singular? error:
> social.fit.diffhomo=ergm.ego(social~edges+nodefactor("acadegree")+nodematch("acadegree",diff=T),control=control.ergm.ego(ppopsize=2000,stats.est="bootstrap",boot.R=20000))
> social.fit.diffhomo=ergm.ego(social~edges+nodefactor("marrital")+nodematch("marrital",diff=T),control=control.ergm.ego(ppopsize=2000,stats.est="bootstrap?,boot.R=20000))

Does it mean this error could emerge when both node factor and node match term are included for the same 2-level factor? If this is the case, what term should I use to test the main effect and the interaction effect (homophily) for a 2-level factor in the same model?

Thank you very much.

Best regards,

YA

messages.subject: [statnet_help] NAs in Bipartite ERGMs
messages.body_plain:
Hello Statnet Team,

I am writing to seek your help with an NA issue in bipartite ergms.  My aim
is to assign attributes to primary and secondary nodes and then calculate
bipartite ergms with these.  My valued network includes 787 primary nodes
and 45 secondary nodes.

So far I have been working with both
1) a complete csv. file including all attributes for primary and secondary
nodes (with NA's) and, also
2) as recommended by Skye Bender de-Moll in a statnet help post (
http://mailman13.u.washington.edu/pipermail/statnet_help/2014/001663.html)
with two separate csv. files for each node set (thus without NA's).

Problem: With both attribute lists I receive an error about NAs after
running ergms.  Any idea what could be wrong?  Here is the code I have been
working with and the error I received.

 net <- network(el, matrix.type="edgelist", bipartite=787, directed=F,
ignore.eval=FALSE,names.eval='Value')

 ## Primary node attributes
pna <- read_csv("Primary node attributes 1492_Bipartite network.csv")
net <- set.vertex.attribute(net, attrname = 'Capital', value=pna$ValueSum,
v=pna$ID)

 ## Secondary node attributes
sna <- read_csv("Secondary node attributes 1492_Bipartite network.csv")
net <- set.vertex.attribute(net, attrname = 'Distance',
value=sna$Greatcircledistance, v=sna$ID)

# ERGM with Error
model1 <- ergm(net ~ edges + b1cov('Capital') + b2cov('Distance'))
Error in ergm.getglobalstats(nw, model, response = response) :
  NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call (arg 13)

Sorry in case this problem is too trivial for this community.  Any help
would be much appreciated.

I would also be very happy about any further information, literature
suggestions about how to do and work with bipartite ergms, interesting
applications etc.

Best wishes,
Bernd



-- 

Bernd Wurpts, M.A. (Magister Artium)
Graduate Student, Ph.D. Candidate
Department of Sociology
University of Washington
http://www.soc.washington.edu/faculty-details/wurpts
wurpts@uw.edu
